context:
Treat bundle and companion files as a binary contract. The `bundle_hash` and
`companion_hashes` fields commit the writer to byte-stable output; honour
that by emitting primary and companion JSON through a single canonical
serializer and hashing the post-serialization bytes. Land in two PRs if
needed: the writer/hash canonicalization first (W1-W3), then the pre-commit
exclusion removal (W4) once the writer is in place and any in-flight bundles
have been re-emitted or grandfathered.
description:
The bundle emitter (`benchbox/core/results/exporter.py`) writes the primary
result JSON and companion `.plans.json` / `.tuning.json` files without a
canonical trailing-newline / whitespace policy. The submit manifest writer
(`benchbox/cli/commands/submit.py`) then records SHA-256 hashes for the
emitted bundle and companions. Tools that round-trip the file —
pre-commit's `end-of-file-fixer` and `trailing-whitespace` hooks, GitHub's
rich JSON viewer, editors that auto-save with a final newline — change
bytes the manifest's `bundle_hash` SHA-256 was computed against.

The W3 corpus-integration PR
(`results-explorer-uat-corpus-integrate-validated-bundles`) hit this when
staging 188 community-submission bundles into `results-data/bundles/`: the
EOF-fixer added trailing newlines and broke every hash. The PR landed by
excluding `results-data/bundles/*.json` from those hooks
(`.pre-commit-config.yaml:106-118`). That fix is correct but it is a
band-aid: any future submitter running a different tool, GitHub PR review
flow, or editor that touches the bytes will hit the same wall, and the
exclusion does not protect them.

The durable fix is to emit the primary bundle and companion JSON files in a
canonical byte-stable form (single serializer with a fixed trailing-newline
policy and stable key ordering) AND compute `bundle_hash` and
`companion_hashes` against that canonical form, so EOF-fixing /
pretty-printing within the canonical form is a no-op.

Originating blind-spot finding:
`_project/blind-spots/2026-05-03-090105-mixed-tooling-data-pr-review-gap.md`.

anti_patterns.dont: canonicalize already-checked-in bundles without also updating their per-bundle manifest hashes
anti_patterns.why: the manifest SHA-256 contract is byte-exact.

anti_patterns.dont: canonicalize the primary bundle while leaving `.plans.json` or `.tuning.json` companions vulnerable
anti_patterns.why: `companion_hashes` are validated by the same manifest path.

anti_patterns.dont: change the manifest's hash function or schema
anti_patterns.instead: only change the writer side, then keep the same SHA-256 contract.
anti_patterns.why: external submitters may already have manifests on disk

anti_patterns.dont: just restore the pre-commit exclusion as 'good enough'
anti_patterns.instead: the durable fix is byte-stable emission.
anti_patterns.why: every future tool that touches bundle bytes will re-trip the hash mismatch

preserves.behavior: All currently checked-in bundles in `results-data/bundles/` continue to validate against `validate_submission.py` before and after the canonicalization rollout.
Per-bundle manifest schema (PR #95) is not changed — only the hash-input bytes change.
Primary bundles, plans companions, and tuning companions are treated consistently.
`bundle_hash` and `companion_hashes` remain SHA-256 hex digests over file bytes; only the emitted bytes are made canonical.
